summary: CCC-built 1934 International Derrick fire tower on Tower Mountain above Cannonsville Reservoir; closed 1989, handed to the Town of Tompkins 2017, closed for climbing during renovations.

facts.design: 72-foot-9-inch International Derrick E-4898 steel fire tower, 1933 model
facts.status_note: Standing; closed for climbing during renovations as of late 2025

access.note: Closed for climbing during renovations (late 2025 information); Wikipedia (Tower Mountain article) says the tower is not safe to climb, but the tower's own Wikipedia article says it may be climbed to just below the cab when the steps are snow-free and weather permits

visit.trail_note: Hike from a parking lot where NYS Routes 10 and 268 meet; parts of the trail cross private and New York City reservoir land, so stay on marked public trails

events.note: Erected by the Civilian Conservation Corps
Lookout operations ended at the end of the 1988 season
Officially closed in early 1989; a 2017 NHLR visit report describes a longer period closed to the public (see resolved_conflicts)
Ownership passed from NYSDEC to the Town of Tompkins; the land belongs to New York City
Added to the National Register of Historic Places, reference 100003231
Summer 2025 project with the Town of Tompkins and NYCDEP; renovation under way, including stair treads and landings
Further rehabilitation planned to continue in summer 2026

corrections.proposed: Town of Tompkins (tower owner since 2017; land owned by New York City)
corrections.why: Wikipedia says the tower was transferred from NYSDEC to the Town of Tompkins in 2017, so the brief's agency is out of date.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and the Rock Rift Wikipedia article give 2,376 ft (724 m); NHLR's description also gives the summit as 2382 ft; the Tower Mountain Wikipedia article gives 2,320 ft (710 m). The brief's 724.2 m matches the majority and is kept.

Wikipedia says the tower was officially closed in early 1989. A 2017 NHLR visit report says it had been closed to the public for many years and reopened only a few years before. The story uses 1989 and reports the disagreement.
Wikipedia dates the transfer to the Town of Tompkins to 2017, and the April 2017 NHLR visit describes the handover as in transition, so 2017 is used.

Komoot (late 2025) says the tower is closed for climbing during renovations, and Tower Mountain's Wikipedia article says it is not safe to climb. The tower's own Wikipedia article says that when the steps are snow free and weather permits, it may be climbed to just below the cab, and that rehabilitation was planned for summer 2026. The story advises against climbing and reports the conflict.

notes_for_editor: The 2025-2026 renovation status rests on a trail guide (Komoot, last updated February 2026) and an FFLA project list; no town notice was found. The NPGallery NRHP page returned only its title, so the NRHP date comes from Wikipedia alone. The brief's coordinates (42.1039, -75.226733) sit several hundred metres from Wikipedia's tower coordinates (42 06 14 N, 75 13 06 W) and from the Tower Mountain summit (42.10944, -75.22611); not changed, so check the pin. No notable fire was found in these sources. The trail length of 3.9 miles from Komoot is not used. Grokipedia and a video appeared in search results and were not used.
